title: The canonical map from extension by zero to direct image for a finite etale morphism
statement:
Let $\pi:U\to X$ be a finite etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $\Lambda$ a commutative ring and $M$ a sheaf of $\Lambda_U$-modules on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $P_M$ be the presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)}M(V,\varphi)$ on $X_{\Et}$ and $\pi_!M=P_M^\#$ its sheafification as a presheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules, $\Lambda_X$ the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] acting on $P_M$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map-linear](2), the extension by zero of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], with sheafification map $\eta_M:P_M\to\pi_!M$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; let $\pi_*M$ be the direct image, $(\pi_*M)(V)=M(V\times_XU)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], a sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules with $\Lambda_X$ acting through $\gamma:\Lambda_X\to\pi_*\Lambda_U$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3); and let $c^p_M:P_M\to\pi_*M$ be the morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map], which is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map-linear](3) (sending $s\in M(V,\varphi)$ to the unique section of $M(V\times_XU)$ that pulls back to $s$ along the graph $\Gamma_\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_V,\varphi)$ and vanishes off $\Gamma_\varphi(V)$).

The *canonical map from extension by zero to direct image* is the unique morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules
$$
c_M:\pi_!M\longrightarrow\pi_*M\qquad\text{with}\qquad c_M\circ\eta_M=c^p_M,
$$
given by the universal property of sheafification. It is natural in $M$: for $\alpha:M\to M'$, $\pi_*\alpha\circ c_M=c_{M'}\circ\pi_!\alpha$, since both sides composed with $\eta_M$ equal $\pi_*\alpha\circ c^p_M=c^p_{M'}\circ P_\alpha$ (naturality of $c^p$ and of $\eta$) and the factorization through $\eta_M$ is unique. (Stacks constructs the same map for every separated etale $\pi$; only the finite etale case is used here.)

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517): 'Sheafification of this map will be the desired map j_!F -> j_*F', on abelian sheaves and sheaves of Lambda-modules; the map of Lemma 03S7 (lemma-shriek-equals-star-finite-etale, line 11571)

proof.text: *The objects are defined.* $P_M$ is the presheaf of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] for $v=\pi$, a presheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$; with $f\in\Lambda_X(V)$ acting on the summand $M(V,\varphi)$ through the ring map $\theta_{V,\varphi}=\Lambda_U(\Gamma_\varphi)\circ\gamma_V:\Lambda_X(V)\to\Lambda_U(V,\varphi)$ it is a presheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map-linear](2). Hence its sheafification $\eta_M:P_M\to\pi_!M=P_M^\#$ as a presheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules exists, $\pi_!M$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules and $\eta_M$ is $\Lambda_X$-linear [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (sheafification of abelian presheaves exists on $X_{\Et}$, which is what that node needs). The direct image $\pi_*M$, $(\pi_*M)(V)=M(V_U,q_V)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], is a sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules with $f\in\Lambda_X(V)$ acting by $\gamma_V(f)$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3), an object of $\Mod(\Lambda_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), proof, first paragraph: 'Sheafification of this map will be the desired map'; sheafification of presheaves of modules: literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex Lemma 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, line 815); module structure on the sum presheaf: sites-modules.tex Lemma 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero, line 2058)

proof.text: *The presheaf map is $\Lambda_X$-linear.* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map](3), $c^p_M:P_M\to\pi_*M$, $c^p_{M,V}((s_\varphi)_\varphi)=\sum_\varphi e_\varphi(s_\varphi)$, is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, i.e. its components commute with the restriction maps; by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map-linear](3) each component $c^p_{M,V}$ is moreover $\Lambda_X(V)$-linear for the structures of step 1. So $c^p_M$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules from $P_M$ to (the presheaf underlying) the sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules $\pi_*M$. (Stacks proves 0F4L for abelian sheaves only and asserts the $\Lambda$-module case; this step and the cited node are the $\Lambda$-module case.)

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), proof, first paragraph: 'Sheafification of this map will be the desired map'; sheafification of presheaves of modules: literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex Lemma 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, line 815); module structure on the sum presheaf: sites-modules.tex Lemma 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero, line 2058)

proof.text: *Existence and uniqueness of $c_M$.* By the universal property of sheafification of presheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], applied to the $\Lambda_X$-linear map $c^p_M$ of step 2 into the sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules $\pi_*M$ of step 1, there is exactly one morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules $c_M:\pi_!M\to\pi_*M$ with $c_M\circ\eta_M=c^p_M$. This is the map of the definition; no choice is involved, so $c_M$ is well defined (up to the choice of the sheafification $(\pi_!M,\eta_M)$, with which it is transported by the unique isomorphism of sheafifications).

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), proof, first paragraph: 'Sheafification of this map will be the desired map'; sheafification of presheaves of modules: literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex Lemma 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, line 815); module structure on the sum presheaf: sites-modules.tex Lemma 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero, line 2058)

proof.text: *$\pi_!$ and $\pi_*$ on morphisms.* Let $\alpha:M\to M'$ be a morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_U$-modules. $P_\alpha=\bigoplus_\varphi\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}:P_M\to P_{M'}$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map-linear](2), and $\pi_!\alpha=P_\alpha^\#$ is the unique morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules with $\pi_!\alpha\circ\eta_M=\eta_{M'}\circ P_\alpha$, the value of the sheafification functor on $P_\alpha$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]; it is the universal property of step 3 applied to $\eta_{M'}\circ P_\alpha$. $\pi_*\alpha$, $(\pi_*\alpha)_V=\alpha_{(V_U,q_V)}$, is a morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules, $\pi_*$ being a functor $\Mod(U_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3), [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), proof, first paragraph: 'Sheafification of this map will be the desired map'; sheafification of presheaves of modules: literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex Lemma 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, line 815); module structure on the sum presheaf: sites-modules.tex Lemma 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero, line 2058)

proof.text: *Naturality in $M$.* For $\alpha:M\to M'$ as in step 4, both $\pi_*\alpha\circ c_M$ and $c_{M'}\circ\pi_!\alpha$ are morphisms of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules $\pi_!M\to\pi_*M'$. Composed with $\eta_M$: $\pi_*\alpha\circ c_M\circ\eta_M=\pi_*\alpha\circ c^p_M$ (step 3) and $c_{M'}\circ\pi_!\alpha\circ\eta_M=c_{M'}\circ\eta_{M'}\circ P_\alpha=c^p_{M'}\circ P_\alpha$ (steps 4 and 3), and $\pi_*\alpha\circ c^p_M=c^p_{M'}\circ P_\alpha$ by the naturality in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map](3). By the uniqueness in the universal property of $\eta_M$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], $\pi_*\alpha\circ c_M=c_{M'}\circ\pi_!\alpha$. Hence $c:\pi_!\to\pi_*$ is a natural transformation of functors $\Mod(U_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ (that $\pi_!$ is a functor, $\pi_!(\beta\alpha)=\pi_!\beta\circ\pi_!\alpha$, $\pi_!\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}$, follows from the same uniqueness).

Gap found: lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map only gives c^p_M as a morphism of presheaves of Lambda-modules, and def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension does not say how Lambda_X acts on P_M; the universal property of def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification needs a Lambda_X-linear map. Factored out as the new node lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map-linear (ring maps theta_{V,phi} = Lambda_U(Gamma_phi) o gamma_V, the Lambda_X-structure on P_M after 03DI, Lambda_X(V)-linearity of e_phi and c^p_M, linearity of P_alpha). noncomputable def Etale.etaleLowerShriekToLowerStar
    (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A) :
    (Etale.etaleLowerShriek A f ‹_›).obj G ⟶ (f)_*[A].obj G
lean.note: The current upstream defines precisely this comparison: the mate under etaleLowerShriekRestrictionAdjunction of lowerStarUnit, whose components are graphExtend (the unique section equal to the input on the graph and zero on its complement). The adjunction is left Kan extension followed by sheafification, so its mate is exactly the unique sheafification factorization of the sum-presheaf graph map. Specialize A to ModuleCat.{u+1} Λ and f to the finite etale π; IsSeparated π follows from IsFinite π. The ModuleCat encoding is authorized by def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves. Naturality follows from lowerStarUnit.naturality and the adjunction homEquiv naturality. No new module or definition.
